entities.name: Adeliza of Louvain
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Adeliza of Louvain (c. 1103–1151) was Queen consort of England as the second wife of King Henry I, and later Countess of Arundel as the wife of William d'Aubigny. She was the daughter of Godfrey I, Count of Louvain and Duke of Lower Lorraine, making her one of the most important marriage alliances Henry I made in his effort to integrate England into the continental European political system.

Her marriage to Henry I in 1121, following the death of Queen Matilda and the catastrophic sinking of the White Ship (1120) that killed Henry's only legitimate son William Adelin, was a desperate attempt to produce a new male heir for the Norman dynasty. Adeliza, though evidently fertile in her second marriage to William d'Aubigny (with whom she had seven children), produced no children with Henry I, contributing to the succession crisis that would engulf England in the civil war known as the Anarchy (1135–1153).

Adeliza was noted as a patron of literature and learning, associated with the Anglo-Norman literary culture that flourished at Henry's court. She commissioned or inspired several works including Philippe de Thaon's Bestiary — one of the earliest Anglo-Norman vernacular texts. Her later years at Arundel Castle placed her at the centre of the Anarchy's conflicts, and her castle was briefly besieged when she gave shelter to the Empress Matilda in 1139.
